chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf who said:

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi Khalid had a slave who was sound and knowledgeable, named Maymun. When death approached him, he bequeathed all his inheritance and possessions to Abu al-Fadl al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, instructing him to convert them into dirhams and send them to Abu Ja'far al-Thani (peace be upon him). The deceased left behind a wife who was pregnant, brothers who had embraced Islam, and a mother who was a Magian. He said: 'I did what he instructed, gathered the dirhams, and delivered them to Muhammad ibn al-Hasan. I resolved to write to him explaining the bequest and the deceased's heirs. Muhammad ibn Bashir and others of our companions advised me not to write an explanation, as he would know the details without it. However, I insisted on writing to him regarding his truthfulness and right. So I wrote, counted the dirhams, and sent them to him. He ordered that one-third be set aside and given to him, and the remainder be returned to his executor to be distributed to his heirs.'
ai.seo_question: How is an estate distributed when the deceased leaves a mix of Muslim and non-Muslim heirs and a pregnant wife?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* illustrates the Imam’s infallible knowledge (*‘ilm al-ghayb* or *‘ilm al-ikhtiyari*) in inheritance matters, as Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ( al-Muqaddam) correctly allocated the one-third bequest portion without needing detailed explanation from the executor. It underscores the Shia legal principle that the Imam’s directive supersedes standard inheritance calculations when he possesses specific knowledge of the deceased's intent or the heirs' circumstances, particularly regarding the distribution to a Magian mother and Muslim siblings.
